incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Articles L.210-1, L.223-1 to L.223-43, and L.223-5 (SARL capital payment rules); implementing rules under Décret n° 2023-431 (electronic formalities).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Paris) / Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) through the single electronic window formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts (Articles of Association) filled in French law form 'M0' (déclaration de constitution de société); registration produces the official Kbis extract.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for SARL; if share capital is fixed, at least one-fifth (20%) of the cash capital must be paid up at the time of incorporation and blocked with a French credit institution until registration and the issuance of the capital deposit certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION — FRANCE SARL [E-COMMERCE ENTITY]. The undersigned founder, acting as sole shareholder of FR SARL, hereby resolves that: (1) the share capital of EUR 1,500 is duly subscribed, fully paid into the company’s designated bank account, and allocated as shares to the sole shareholder; (2) the registered office is adopted at 128 Rue de la Convention, 75015 Paris, with jurisdiction of the Paris Commercial Court; (3) the Gérant (Manager) is appointed as legal representative with authority to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and represent the company; (4) the company’s object includes online retail and wholesale distribution of portable solar generators and photovoltaic accessories, ISIC 4791; and (5) the Manager shall complete all registrations, licenses, and tax formalities. Adopted unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI – Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (online trademark and corporate name clearance portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name and trademark availability search on the INPI data portal; reserve the proposed legal name and corresponding domain name where available; retain the negative certificate and domain registration certificate for inclusion in the statutory filing package.
required_dossiers: Proposed legal name and domain name
Identity document of the founding manager
Precise business activity description (ISIC 4791)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused due to conflict with an existing trademark or protected commercial term, select an amended name and resubmit a new clearance request with the amended articles of association.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel / notary (optional, but mandatory when an in-kind real property contribution is made)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the French Statuts in accordance with Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 of the Commercial Code; ensure clauses on corporate purpose, registered office, share capital, class of shares, governance, and dispute resolution; have all shareholders initial every page and sign the final execution copy.
required_dossiers: Signed statutory articles
Valuation report by a statutory auditor if in-kind contribution is made
Valid passport or national identity card of each shareholder
Personal address and nationality statements of shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar queries the corporate purpose or capital clauses, convene an extraordinary shareholders’ meeting to amend the articles and file a rectified execution copy before resubmitting the incorporation application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Deposit and Blocking at a French Credit Institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French retail bank or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (blocked capital account provider)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional corporate capital account in the name of the company being formed; deposit at least 20% of the subscribed cash capital; obtain an attestation de dépôt des fonds (capital deposit certificate) from the bank; the funds must remain blocked until the company is inscribed in the commercial registry.
required_dossiers: Draft statutes
Identity documents and KYC evidence of shareholders
Bank onboarding forms and source-of-funds declaration
Proof of the registered address for account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines to open the account, select an alternative eligible financial institution and obtain a new deposit certificate; any change in the depositary bank requires an updated capital deposit certificate included in the final registration file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Legal Formation Notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d’annonces légales (JAL) authorized in the département of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish a statutory legal notice in an authorized legal gazette containing the corporate name, legal form, capital, registered office address, corporate object, manager’s name, and commercial registry designation; obtain the justificatif de publication (proof of publication) issued by the gazette.
required_dossiers: Projected text of the legal notice
Final draft of the statutes
INPI name compatibility certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the gazette rejects the notice for missing mandatory particulars, correct the notice and republish; the new publication certificate must be used when responding to the registry query.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of the Incorporation File to the Electronic Formalities Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet électronique des formalités des entreprises – INPI via formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create a user account, fill out the M0 declaration, upload scanned copies of identity documents, statutes, bank capital certificate, publication certificate, address proof, and declaration of no insolvency or management ban; pay the registry and INPI statutory fees; track the application in the platform until the Kbis extract is delivered.
required_dossiers: Completed M0 declaration form
Signed and dated statutes (certified copy)
Capital deposit certificate from the bank
Legal notice publication certificate
Affidavit of no personal insolvency and no judicial management ban
Proof of registered office address
Identity documents of shareholders and manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query (demande de complément), respond within 15 days using the online rectification module; supplement the file with the missing documentation and pay any additional correction fee published by the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Regulatory Activation and Kbis Delivery
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI / Infogreffe and URSSAF / Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the registration certificate and Kbis extract are issued, file the beneficial ownership declaration with the commercial registry, complete the URSSAF employer registration, obtain the completed SIRET status confirmation, and activate VAT and social contribution statuses for the new entity.
required_dossiers: Registration certificate (Kbis)
Beneficial ownership declaration (déclarant des bénéficiaires effectifs)
Final bank account details
Copy of the incorporation file receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis contains erroneous data, file an online rectification request with the Greffe within 8 days; if URSSAF activation is delayed, follow up via the URSSAF online portal and present the registration certificate as evidence.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – no industrial or manufacturing permit is required for an ISIC 4791 online direct retail business without on-site production.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No specific operating licence; however, general consumer protection and e-commerce duties under Articles L.111-1, L.121-16 and L.511-1 of the French Consumer Code apply, together with the legal warranty and information obligations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition écologique / DREAL coordinated with ADEME
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – pure online retail of portable battery generators and photovoltaic accessories is not listed as a project requiring a formal environmental impact assessment or registration under the French environmental code (L.181-1 and annex to Article R.122-2).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to office-only operations. Extended producer responsibility obligations apply to portable batteries and electrical equipment placed on the EU market: compliance with EU Regulation 2023/1542 (batteries) and Articles R.543-52 et seq. of the French Environmental Code, including WEEE registration, battery collection, recycling financing, and quarterly sales reporting to the national registries.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No civil-defense permit is required for non-manufacturing e-commerce. If the company operates an office or incidental warehouse, fire safety certification for ERP (établissement recevant du personnel) is required under Articles R.123-1 et seq. of the Code de la construction et de l’habitation; electrical installations must comply with NF-C 15-100 standards, and the company must register with DREETS for occupational health and provide basic workplace safety clearance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), administered through the Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) and, for non-resident businesses, the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères (SIEE); official portal: impots.gouv.fr. Company formation and registration filings are submitted through the Guichet unique operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI), which transmits data to the tax administration. The company receives a SIREN and establishment-level SIRET; a French VAT identification number is issued by the DGFiP.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate the SARL and file the formation formalities through the INPI Guichet unique. 2. Obtain the SIREN/SIRET and identify the competent SIE from the registration record. 3. Submit the VAT liability and tax-option information through the company formation filing or directly to the competent SIE using the required business tax registration forms. 4. Provide the articles of association, Kbis or registration extract, registered office evidence, bank details, director identification, beneficial-owner information, business activity description, projected turnover, and evidence of taxable transactions where requested. 5. The DGFiP assigns the French VAT number in the format FR plus two control characters and the nine-digit SIREN. 6. Validate the VAT number through the European Commission VIES system for intra-Community transactions. 7. Register separately for an EORI number through French customs before importing or exporting goods. A foreign company without a French establishment applies through the SIEE or the competent non-resident tax channel. Businesses established in another EU Member State generally do not need a fiscal representative in France; businesses established outside the EU generally must appoint an accredited French fiscal representative unless an applicable mutual-assistance exception or special regime applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A French SARL is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, or IS) on its taxable profits. The standard territorial rules apply, including taxation of French business activity, French permanent establishments, and specified French-source income. A qualifying small company may benefit from the reduced corporate income tax rate on a specified first tranche of profit, subject to ownership, turnover, and capital-payment conditions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: There is no general US-style check-the-box election. A SARL may elect corporate income tax where it is otherwise eligible for income-tax treatment, and a qualifying SARL may elect temporary income-tax transparency under Article 239 bis AB of the French Tax Code, generally for up to five financial years and subject to statutory conditions concerning age, size, ownership, voting rights, activity, and capital holding. A family SARL may elect income-tax treatment under the family-company regime, subject to qualifying family ownership and activity conditions. These elections are formal statutory options, not unrestricted entity-classification elections. French anti-hybrid-mismatch rules may deny deductions or impose inclusion where arrangements produce deduction-without-inclusion or double-deduction outcomes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT), supplemented for eligible cross-border e-commerce by the Union One Stop Shop (OSS), Import One Stop Shop (IOSS), and customs import VAT procedures.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a French-established retailer supplying goods domestically, the ordinary franchise en base threshold is generally EUR 85,000 of prior-year turnover, with a tolerance threshold generally EUR 93,500 for the current year, subject to the applicable statutory period and legislative changes. A business exceeding the relevant threshold, opting for VAT, making transactions that are not eligible for the franchise, importing goods, or undertaking certain intra-Community and cross-border transactions may require VAT registration irrespective of the domestic small-business threshold. For intra-Community distance sales of goods and certain electronically supplied services to EU consumers, the EU-wide EUR 10,000 threshold applies, after which French or OSS reporting may be required. The 20% standard rate applies to most portable power generators, batteries, and solar panels sold in France, subject to product-specific reduced-rate rules that must be separately verified.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory electronic invoicing and transaction e-reporting through accredited Partner Dematerialization Platforms (PDPs), with a public directory and designated data-routing infrastructure. The current statutory timetable provides that all businesses must be able to receive electronic invoices from 1 September 2026; issuance obligations generally begin on 1 September 2026 for large and medium-sized enterprises and on 1 September 2027 for small and micro-enterprises, subject to legislative or regulatory amendments. Domestic B2B invoices within the scope of the mandate must use structured or hybrid electronic formats and contain the required transaction, VAT, identification, payment, and status data. France does not currently operate a universal real-time pre-clearance model for all invoices. Transaction e-reporting applies principally to B2C and cross-border transactions outside the domestic B2B e-invoicing flow. B2C e-commerce invoices are not generally subject to mandatory issuance in every retail transaction unless required by the customer or applicable sector rules. Customs declarations and import/export records are filed electronically through the French and EU customs systems.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from France to a destination outside the European Union may be invoiced without French VAT where the supplier, carrier, customs representative, or buyer completes the export formalities and the supplier retains evidence that the goods actually exited the EU customs territory. The supplier must establish the link between the invoice, the goods, the customs declaration, and the exit confirmation. Intra-Community supplies to a VAT-identified customer in another EU Member State may qualify for the French VAT exemption where the customer has a valid VAT number, the goods are dispatched to another Member State, and the supplier satisfies documentary, reporting, and recapitulative-statement requirements. Services supplied to a business customer established outside France are generally governed by the place-of-supply rules and may be outside the scope of French VAT rather than zero-rated; service qualification, customer status, and use-and-enjoyment rules must be documented. Export VAT refunds require valid purchase invoices, proof of VAT payment, business use, and compliance with the applicable refund or VAT-return procedure.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Commercial invoice identifying the seller, buyer, goods, values, Incoterms, and VAT treatment
Electronic customs export declaration containing the Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Export acceptance and exit confirmation from the EU customs system, including the electronic proof of exit or equivalent customs certification
Packing list and transport documentation, such as bill of lading, air waybill, courier record, or road consignment note
Evidence linking the goods and transport to the VAT invoice, including serial numbers or shipment references where commercially relevant
Proof of the purchaser and destination outside the EU, where required by the transaction and risk profile
For intra-Community supplies, the customer VAT identification number, transport evidence, and required recapitulative statement

Bank payment evidence or commercial settlement records where relevant to substantiate the transaction; a French inward-remittance certificate is not a general statutory requirement for export VAT exemption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general foreign-exchange control rule requiring export proceeds to be repatriated within 180 days. Export proceeds should nevertheless be traceable through ordinary accounting, banking, customs, and anti-money-laundering records. If an export exemption or zero-rating claim is unsupported, the DGFiP may reassess the VAT that should have been charged, deny input VAT recovery connected with the transaction, and impose late-payment interest generally calculated at the statutory monthly rate, currently 0.20% per month, subject to applicable rules. Additional penalties may include 10% for certain late or deficient filings, 40% for deliberate non-compliance, and up to 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres or abuse of rights. Fraudulent or deliberately false customs or tax documentation may also trigger customs sanctions, criminal tax-fraud exposure, director or officer liability, and loss of simplified customs or VAT privileges. The taxpayer should retain export and transport evidence for the applicable French accounting and tax limitation periods, commonly at least three years for VAT assessment purposes and longer where accounting or customs retention rules apply.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France adheres to the Eurozone monetary framework with unrestricted capital and current account convertibility. All profit remittances, dividends, and capital repatriations are permitted without prior approval or surrender requirements. No capital controls apply to resident French entities under EU directives.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender of export proceeds is required under EU regulations. Export receipts denominated in EUR may be retained in full. Non-EU exports require standard customs declaration and statistical reporting but impose no conversion obligation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Limited feasibility for cross-border electronic money institution activities. French ACPR licensing is mandatory for any EMI providing payment services; offshore digital EMIs are not permitted without specific authorization and full compliance with PSD2 and open banking rules.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital KYC and account opening is permitted for standard corporate clients through approved platforms. Physical presence or video interview is required only for enhanced due diligence cases or monthly transaction volumes exceeding EUR 50,000.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Extract from French national registry (Infogreffe) confirming ownership percentages and identities of all shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners
Bank statements, corporate tax returns, and audited financial statements for the preceding 24 months demonstrating legitimate business operations

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital via SEPA Instant or standard SEPA transfers to French IBAN accounts. Use purpose codes 'CAP' or 'EQTY' for equity injections. All transfers require supporting documentation including beneficial ownership certificates and source-of-funds evidence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing through SWIFT MT103 for international trade settlements. EU trade uses SEPA; non-EU transactions employ correspondent banking with Commercial Letters of Credit where required. All disbursements must reference commercial invoices, contracts, and regulatory purpose codes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing (deposit of financial statements, management report, and audit report if applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the fiscal year (e.g., 31 December year-end -> 30 June)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Daily late penalty of EUR 50; court fine up to EUR 1,500; administrative strike-off from RCS after formal notice

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale, IS) and mandatory e-filing of financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Second business day after 1 May for calendar-year entities, or within one month after approval of accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late filing penalty plus monthly interest of 0.20%; potential 5% per 6 months for non-payment

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Two of three thresholds: turnover > EUR 8,000,000, balance sheet > EUR 4,000,000, average workforce > 50; optional by shareholder request
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (PCG - Plan Comptable Général); IFRS only for consolidated accounts

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO confirmation; RCS beneficial-owner declaration must be updated within 30 days of any change (e.g., shareholding transfers). Annual accounts filing evidences ongoing data accuracy.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of movements of shares (registre des mouvements de titres)
Register of decisions of the manager/shareholders

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D tax credit (5-30% of eligible costs), innovation status (statut de l'innovation) tax benefits, export rebates

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1200-A (Déclaration de résultat) via impots.gouv.fr electronic portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 3 months after fiscal year-end (e.g., 31 March for 31 December year-end)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report French-sourced income only; non-residents file specific procedures

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses and cost of sales
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductible expenses require substantiation; limited to French PE for non-residents
Apply transfer pricing and thin capitalization rules where relevant

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: 0.75% of tax due per month of delay (minimum €70, maximum 10% of tax due) plus interest on unpaid tax

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% between French companies; 12.8% for non-resident shareholders (reduced by DTAs to 0-15%)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit TRC and DTA claim form via impots.gouv.fr; processing typically 2-4 weeks
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% under EU directives or treaties; Interest: 12.8% statutory, reduced to 0% under most treaties

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: €50 million group turnover; Master File: €750 million group turnover
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France enforces economic substance under ATAD and DAC6 for holding, IP and finance entities; non-compliance results in deduction disallowance

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of income or false declarations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 80% of evaded tax penalty plus criminal prosecution; up to 5 years imprisonment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal fines, disqualification from management roles, and criminal liability

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain or file TP documentation or apply arm's length principle
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties up to 500% of adjustment amount plus interest on additional tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil restitution claims and potential criminal tax fraud charges

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining entity without real business activity or French substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of tax deductions, recharacterization, and fines up to €10,000
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Imprisonment up to 5 years and fines for fraudulent management
